entry.narrative_markdown:
## Question
Do independent records confirm or refute that Catherine Donovan was the wife of Patrick Hoban, born about 1836 in Halifax, Nova Scotia?

## Conclusion
The evidence strongly supports that Catherine Donovan (born about 1847) was the wife of Patrick Hoban (born about 1836, Halifax). They married at Halifax on 18 November 1867, and she is named as the mother of their four children baptised 1868-1875. No record names a different wife. The finding is probable, not proved, because every record read is an index entry rather than an examined original register, and census and death records remain unsearched.

## Evidence
**Marriage entries.** Five index entries record the 18 Nov 1867 marriage of Patrick Hoban, age 31, son of Richard Hoban and Margaret (Kilfoyle), to Catherine Donovan, age 20, daughter of Daniel Donovan: three in "Canada, Nova Scotia, Marriages, 1864-1918" (FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:WHMT-NGW2, 1:1:W4YS-94N2, 1:1:DX6P-6YT2), one in "Canada, Marriages, 1661-1949" (1:1:XL58-SXH) and one in "Canada, Nova Scotia, Church Records, 1720-2001" (1:1:DSXQ-GZ6Z). A sixth, "Canada, Nova Scotia, Vital Records, 1763-1957" (1:1:KMLR-9D8), lists Patrick Hoban and Catherine Donavan as spouses in 1868. Classification: derivative indexes of original registers; the names, ages and marriage date are primary information given by the parties themselves, parents' names are secondary information. Caution on independence: the first four entries cite shared register images (for example image ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89N6-89DM is cited by three of them), so they are best treated as several indexings of one civil register entry. The church register entry is a separate record-creating process, and the vital-records entry is a further index.

**Baptisms.** Four church baptism entries, each a separate event and entry in "Canada, Nova Scotia, Church Records, 1720-2001": Richard Michael Hobin (23 Oct 1868, 1:1:D3SK-ZGPZ), John William Hobin (7 Jan 1871, 1:1:CYTN-816Z), Thomas Patrick Hoban (20 Feb 1873, 1:1:4YDS-2LN2) and Mary May Margaret Hobin (10 May 1875, 1:1:417B-HQN2). Each names the father as Patrick Hoban or Hobin and the mother as Catherine Donovan or Donivan. This is indirect evidence of the marriage and independent of the marriage register.

**Identity.** The groom's stated age (31) and Halifax birthplace match the tree subject born 1836; person-evidence matches against the tree subject score 0.96 to 0.98 for the marriage personas.

## Conflicts and the alternative wife
No registered conflict exists. Bride's mother is given as Mary (src 1:1:W4YS-94N2), Margaret (1:1:WHMT-NGW2) and Margaret McCarthy (1:1:DSXQ-GZ6Z); this is a variation in a secondary detail across informants and indexers and does not bear on whether the bride is the same Catherine Donovan. The objective raised the possibility of a wife named Ellen. A search for a marriage of a Patrick Hoban to an Ellen in Nova Scotia 1855-1867 found none in the FamilySearch index. The only Ellen lead is the 17 June 1895 Halifax marriage of Thomas Dee (about 21) and Bessie Butler, which names his parents as Patrick and Ellen (ark:/61903/1:1:DXFG-GM3Z and 1:1:WQLS-7K3Z). Thomas Dee scored 0.016 against Patrick Hoban in matching and appeared in the 1881 census in the household of a Patrick Dee, so he is treated as the son of a different Patrick, with a different surname, and not as a child of this couple. None of the Hoban children is named Thomas Dee; Thomas Patrick Hoban (baptised 1873) is a separate person and no record links him to the Dee marriage.

## Limits
The tier is probable because (1) all sources are derivative indexes and the register images were not examined, and (2) the 1871 and 1881 census households and a death or burial record naming a spouse have not been searched; each would corroborate the answer and is reachable through FamilySearch. The negative search for an Ellen is limited to one index.

## Tree
The tree already carries the Couple relationship between Patrick Hoban (KK3W-WLT) and Catherine Donovan (KK3W-WLB) with the 18 Nov 1867 Halifax marriage fact, and ParentChild links to the four children. The marriage fact now carries source references to the six record entries.
